Research Contributions

Innovations in Electromagnetics

Professor Qaisar Abbas Naqvi is a leading researcher on the Kobayashi Potential Method (KPM) in Electromagnetics.

Our group has successfully applied KPM to classical geometries (strip, slit, disk, hole) and developed mathematical models for scattering in complex media including Lorentz-Drude, chiral, and topological insulator mediums.

Kobayashi Potential Method

A rigorous mathematical technique for mixed boundary value problems. We have extended KPM to analyze scattering from classical geometries like strips, slits, and disks in complex non-integer dimensional spaces.

Metamaterials & Optics

Studying metamaterials as a platform for field manipulation. Our models describe propagation in Lorentz-Drude, Chiral, and Topological Insulator media, offering applications in both civil and military domains.

Tunable Optical Shifts

Exploring the Goos-Hänchen (GH) shift in Graphene and Epsilon-Near-Zero (ENZ) slabs. Our studies show these shifts can be actively controlled, aiding the design of advanced photonic sensors and switches.

Ghost Waves

Pioneering work on non-uniform electromagnetic waves that combine characteristics of both propagating and evanescent waves. These "Ghost Waves" open new avenues in dielectric magnetic anisotropic materials.

Publications & Bibliography

Academic Record • Books • Journals

Professor Naqvi has authored over 100+ peer-reviewed journal papers and several book chapters. His work is widely cited in the fields of fractional electromagnetics and metamaterials.

Springer

Electromagnetic Fields and Waves in Fractional Dimensional Space

Qaisar Abbas Naqvi, M. Zubair, M. J. Mughal

SpringerBriefs in Applied Sciences and Technology, 2012.

A comprehensive mathematical framework for solving boundary value problems in non-integer dimensions. This seminal text bridges the gap between classical electromagnetics and fractional calculus.

Teaching & Mentorship

Graduate & Undergraduate Courses

Professor Naqvi is dedicated to training the next generation of engineers. His teaching philosophy emphasizes rigorous mathematical foundations paired with physical intuition.

Graduate Courses (MS/PhD)

EE-601

Advanced Electromagnetic Theory

A comprehensive study of Maxwell’s equations, Green’s functions, and wave propagation in anisotropic and chiral media.

EE-604

Methods of Mathematical Physics

Focusing on complex variables, partial differential equations, and integral transforms used in advanced engineering problems.

EE-720

Scattering & Diffraction

Advanced techniques for solving scattering problems, including Physical Optics (PO) and the Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD).

Undergraduate Courses

EE-301

Electromagnetic Field Theory

Fundamental concepts of electrostatics, magnetostatics, and time-varying fields for junior engineering students.

EE-210

Linear Circuit Analysis

Core principles of circuit theory, network theorems, and transient analysis in time and frequency domains.
